newsitem.title: UK: Briton convicted of machete attack on children.
newsitem.headline: Briton convicted of machete attack on children.

text.p: A British man obsessed by the Dunblane massacre of 16 children in March was found guilty on Monday of invading a nursery school playground in central England and attacking youngsters with a machete.

Horrett Campbell, 33, was found guilty of seven charges of attempted murder at Stafford Crown Court. He was ordered to be detained at a high security mental hospital for three months before sentencing.
Campbell, an unemployed welder, told the court he launched the attack on July 8 during a playground picnic because he believed that the children at the school were calling him names.
None of the children was killed but one boy had his skull broken by a blow from the two-foot-long (50 cm) machete.
Described as a paranoid schizophrenic, Campbell was obsessed by Thomas Hamilton, who shot dead 16 children and their teacher in the Scottish town of Dunblane before killing himself, the court heard.
Campbell felt victimised by society after hearing voices in his head telling him the pupils at the school were devils. He set out, like Hamilton, to "get even" and become a mass murderer.

Judge Stephen Sedley said he would recommend that nursery nurse Lisa Potts, 21, who was seriously injured by blows from Campbell's machete as she tried to shield the children, be put forward for a bravery award.
